- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent 18-day max), apply a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–5% per day until price stabilizes.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 18-day moving average), adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply a 2–4% downward bias correction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67), reduce forecast slope to avoid “over-leveraged” extrapolation.  
- If forecast is > 10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply a “cooling-off” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until convergence.
